name: text-unicode
algorithm: One std.text function (graphemes, width, the four normalization forms, full case folding), reps passes over the generated text of ../utf16/README.md (splitmix64 from seed, mib MiB, 37.5 percent of the scalars outside ASCII); mode marks: Nfd of a then mib * 2^20 combining marks of four classes cycling; README.md.

skip.c: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, case folding or width: C has none
skip.rust: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, case folding or width: unicode-segmentation, unicode-normalization and unicode-width are crates; no crate stands in
skip.zig: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, case folding or width: Zig's std.unicode has UTF-8 and UTF-16 only
skip.go: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, full case folding or width: golang.org/x/text and rivo/uniseg are not std (Go's unicode.SimpleFold is simple folding only); no module stands in
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the functions' arithmetic cannot overflow

variants.name: marks1
notes: Nfd of "a" then 2^20 combining marks of four classes cycling (README.md): the worst case of canonical ordering (TEXT2-3).

variants.name: marks4
notes: As marks1 with 2^22 marks: a linear reorder takes about 4 times marks1.

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, and this one has the Mk column only; the checksum (clusters, columns, or the result's length and one byte a pass) checks the run
notes: Mk-only throughput rows: no standard library among C, Rust, Zig and Go has these facilities (skip), so there is no ratio; bytes per second = mib * 1048576 * reps / median.
